_README.purpose: Evidence bundle for the eval_fix accuracy question. Self-contained: every published number can be recomputed from this file.
how_to_verify: The eval_fix verdict uses a 10000-sample bootstrap over the per-pair delta_cindex values (seed 0, numpy default_rng).
curve_peak.best_epoch is the argmax of val_cindex_exploratory over epochs where val_cindex_status == 'computed'.

omitted_and_why.per_patient_risks_and_logits: eval_repeats.json is ~243 KB per arm, dominated by per-patient risk vectors. C-index per repeat is retained; the raw vectors are not needed to recompute any claim and would take the bundle from 1 MB to 130 MB.
omitted_and_why.checkpoints_last_pt_and_shared_initial_s: 821 files, 8.9 GB total. Only the sha256 provenance hashes are retained.
omitted_and_why.patient_slot_intervention_json: 2.8 MB per arm, not referenced by any conclusion in RESULTS.md.

headline.question: Does eval_fix systematically cost C-index accuracy?
headline.interpretation: No systematic effect detected. The CI spans zero and both signs occur. This does NOT prove absence of an effect: the upper bound is +0.0068, so any true penalty smaller than that would be undetectable at n=18.

critical_limitation.finding: All checkpoints used are past their own optimum.
critical_limitation.consequence: The eval_fix verdict therefore describes the OVERFITTED regime. Behaviour at the model's own optimum was never measured. This is the main limitation of this study and is stated as such in RESULTS.md.
